data.component: WAN NIC (vtnet0) transmit path / virtio driver on the firewall
data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a wedged transmit queue (repeated "vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flaps), so nothing can be sent out the WAN — outbound packets fail with ENOBUFS ("No buffer space available") and the ISP gateway ARP stays incomplete — even though the cable modem recovered and reports OPERATIONAL; the WAN watchdog hit its 12-reload cap and stopped, but those reloads only re-ran dhclient over the stuck interface.
evidence: dmesg -a shows repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interspersed with 'link state changed to DOWN/UP', indicating a hung TX queue on the WAN NIC
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 -n 8.8.8.8 both fail with 'sendto: No buffer space available' (ENOBUFS) and 100% loss — traffic cannot leave the WAN
arp -a -n shows the ISP gateway 198.51.100.1 as '(incomplete)' while the LAN host 10.20.0.9 resolves and pings fine (0% loss), isolating the fault to the WAN path
netstat -i shows vtnet0 with 48211 output errors (Oerrs)

/var/log/system/latest.log: dpinger 'WAN_DHCP 198.51.100.1: sendto error: 55' at 02:01:58, and every wan-watchdog reload is followed by dhclient 'send_packet: No buffer space available' (02:30, 02:40, 03:25) — DHCP renewals could not be sent over the stuck interface
/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl: outage since ~02:01, 12 reloads in 24h reached max_reloads_24h=12, so watchdog took action=none (reload_cap) at 03:30

modem-events.jsonl/modem-metrics.jsonl: modem logged 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44 then 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21 and status OPERATIONAL since — the provider side recovered, so the remaining fault is on the firewall's WAN NIC
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 transmit queue and recover the WAN path. A wan_reload alone will not help: the logs show repeated reloads already failed with ENOBUFS because the NIC TX path itself is wedged, and the modem has already re-registered and reports OPERATIONAL. Note the maintainer is away tonight, so this reboot needs their approval before it can be run; a modem_reboot would not address the cause. Once back up, investigate the virtio driver watchdog timeouts (and consider raising the watchdog reload cap or adding an interface-reset step) so a future hang self-recovers without waiting on a maintainer.
